list.expr: {job="juno"} |= "Juno is a Go implementation of a Starknet full-node client created by Nethermind."
list.name: Node Start

panels.description: Blocks and transactions that sync stores per second.
panels.title: Sync Speed

panels.description: Average time that one block spends in each step. fetch, verify and store are work. fetchWait and verifyWait are the time that a finished block waits for the blocks before it. Fetch and verify run in parallel, so the sum is not the time between two stored blocks.
panels.title: Average Time per Block, by Step

panels.description: Block fetches that run now. In catch-up mode the limit is min(16, GOMAXPROCS). A value below the limit means that fetch workers wait for the in-order queue.
panels.title: 1. Fetches in Flight

panels.description: Time to download one block, its state update and its new classes, and to convert them. At the chain tip it also includes the time that sync waits for the next block.
panels.title: 1. Fetch Latency

panels.description: New classes that block fetches download per second, and the average download time of all classes in one block. The time includes only blocks with new classes.
panels.title: 1b. Class Downloads

panels.description: Time that a finished block waits before the next step takes it. Blocks leave each step in order, so one slow block makes all blocks after it wait. A block also waits when the queue of the next step is full, so a slow verify or store also shows here.
panels.title: 2. Queue Wait

panels.description: Part of the fetch time of a block that it spends in the queue after its download. A high value means that the network does not limit sync: a slow earlier block, or a slow verify or store, holds the fetched blocks.
panels.title: 2. Fetch Time Spent Waiting

panels.description: Time to verify the block hash and commitments, and time to store one block.
panels.title: 3. Verify and 4. Store Latency

panels.description: Average time of one block store, in two parts. commit is the write to disk. state + block write is the rest: the state and trie update with the root hash, and the block content write. db_commit_latency also counts commits that are not from sync, so the split is approximate.
panels.title: 4. Store Time by Part (avg)

panels.description: Time of each database batch commit, with fsync.
panels.title: 5. DB Commit Latency

panels.description: Write stalls per second, by cause. Any value above zero slows down store.
panels.title: 5. DB Write Stalls

panels.description: Bytes that compaction must still rewrite, and the L0 sublevel count. High values come before write stalls.
panels.title: 5. Compaction Debt and L0 Sublevels

panels.description: go_memstats_lookups_total – counts how many pointer dereferences happened. This is a counter value so you can use rate() to lookups/s.
panels.title: CPU Usage (Single Core %)
Pebble Block Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Part of block reads that the Pebble block cache serves.

targets.legendFormat: bytes of memory are used for other runtime allocations

panels.description: shows how many heap objects are allocated. This is a counter value so you can use rate() to objects allocated/s.
panels.title: GO Rate of Objects Allocated
